STATED BY ANTHONY 2026-08-09, AND IT BREAKS THE ANSWER THE 2026-08-06 NODE SETTLED ON.

=== THE ACCESS TOPOLOGY, FINALLY EXPLICIT ===

"My brother will be co-developing flo2 and we'll both have access to and work from the flo2 github repo. He doesn't have access to the other repos though (maybe reflow2, but I don't think so — he just installs it the standard manner and gives me feedback on it)."

  flo2 (C)     TWO WRITERS on one shared git repo — the multi-writer merge case dec:multi-writer-architecture was built for
  reflow2 (B)  ONE WRITER, plus a consumer who installs the released kit and reports back. NO repo access.
  A, D         Anthony only.

⇒ The brother is a CONSUMER of reflow2 and a CO-AUTHOR of flo2, and those are different relationships needing different mechanisms. His reflow2 feedback already arrives the way `dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency` predicts a consumer's would — out of band, by hand, with nothing in either graph knowing.

=== ⚠️⚠️ THE HOSTED CASE, WHICH THE GIT ANSWER DOES NOT REACH ===

"Some of this discussion may come into particular value in flo2 if we have MULTIPLE USERS AND MULTIPLE PROJECTS, SOME OF WHICH ARE DEPENDENT UPON OTHER'S PROJECTS WITHIN THE SAME DYNOGRAPH-FOUNDATION DB."

THAT IS A DIFFERENT TOPOLOGY, NOT A BIGGER ONE. The 2026-08-06 answer — file a proposed node on a BRANCH of the upstream's repo, merged by its owner — rests on three things the hosted case does not have:
  (1) a git repo per design. In flo2 there is one shared database, not N repos.
  (2) a branch and a merge as the review gate. A shared db has no branch to file against.
  (3) the filer and the owner being the same KIND of party. Here they are different TENANTS.

⇒ **THE TRANSPORT THAT MAKES THE REPO CASE COST ZERO NEW CODE IS UNAVAILABLE IN THE HOSTED CASE.** The 2026-08-06 node half-anticipated this — "for the HOSTED case flo2's own layer must be the mailbox" — but treated it as a deployment detail. With cross-TENANT dependencies it is not a detail: it is a second mechanism, and the one that has to be designed rather than inherited.

⭐ AND IT MAKES THE COMPARTMENT QUESTION LOAD-BEARING. `dec:idea-need-to-know-compartments` asks whether per-user graph scope is a convenience or a COMPARTMENT. In the repo world that is abstract — each person holds their own clone. In one shared db where user X's project depends on user Y's, an automatic cross-project write is a channel BETWEEN TENANTS, and the safe direction is defined against SENSITIVITY rather than against the dependency arrow. A levied requirement is a write into someone else's design by someone who is not their collaborator.

⚠️ ONE THING THAT DOES CARRY OVER, AND IT IS THE SAFETY PROPERTY: the repo answer is safe partly BECAUSE it never opens the upstream's store — it is a diff against a committed file, so it cannot move their schema stamp (see `fact:the-five-project-census-2026-08-09`: dynograph-foundation still stamps 0.16.0, and opening it with a current binary would upgrade it). **In a shared db every write opens the store by definition.** So the hosted mailbox must supply, by other means, the isolation the file transport gets for free.

NOTHING IS DECIDED. This records that `dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency` has TWO environments and only one of them has an answer — which the options as written do not distinguish.
